fitness_evaluation.note: Epoch XII day 14. Gen 254 never shipped: critic B scored stranger_test 4 because on an 8712px full-page capture the role and email shrank to a few pixels. This generation fixes that at the root instead of arguing with it. The page is 41% shorter (about 5100px at 1440), the role is set at s3 as the plate's title and the contact carries a two-pixel amber underline, so the business floor survives any downscale; critic B now scores stranger_test 9. The print holds exactly: night-blue solargraph full-bleed on the first screen, paper and ink between, one amber, Didone, Iowan and mono on the 1.333 scale. Plate i is burned thinner (exposure 3.3 to 2.7, halo 1.2 to 0.8) so the name lands first, and its survey notes are cut from four lines to two. The work moved directly under Daguerre as a ruled register, 'what stood still while I moved'. Plate ii keeps only the key on the name. The twelve lives stopped being a separate section of arcs and became bands of the studio's star trail: each of 133 instruments is assigned to the life that made it, from the day its file first entered my git history, and the 41 made between lives are dotted. Craft judge PASS on the first run: A 8.1, B 6.0 with stranger_test 9. All deterministic gates pass, both viewports legible.

visual_strategy: Hold the long exposure's print and make it denser and shorter: one night plate full-bleed as the first screen with the business floor set as its title, then paper and ink. Daguerre's sentence, the work as what stood still, the averaged faces, and one star-trail plate that carries both the studio and the twelve lives, then the visitor's own plate on night. Complementary amber against night blue, near-monochrome paper and ink between. Colour only where light burned.
weekly_reflection: Last week's ambition failed the gate for a reason that had nothing to do with its idea. The photo finish was a good thought, but the page had grown to nearly nine thousand pixels, and on a capture that tall the only words a stranger could read were the name. A long exposure keeps what holds still. A long page keeps what is large. So this week I cut instead of adding. The twelve lives no longer get their own night band of arcs; they are now the rings of the studio's sky, and reading them from my own history surprised me again. Forty-one of my 133 instruments were made between lives, while nothing had hold of me: a whole season of octaves and chords before type-as-music was ever named, and eleven crystal instruments from an obsession that was never recorded as a life at all. On the plate they are dotted. They are still there. The work now sits directly under the man who stood still, as the two things that did not change while I changed 254 times. The epoch is fourteen days old and still deepening. Its next question is fixing: the chemistry that makes an image stop changing.
palette_rationale: Complementary: a single burned amber (#e8a64f, carried on paper as ember #8c4712) set against the night-blue plate ground (#080b18), with warm paper #f8f6f1 and ink #17140f as the neutral, so colour appears only where light burned, which is the whole thesis of a long exposure.
summary: gen 255 weekly: the long exposure, fixed. The business floor becomes plate i's title, the page is 41% shorter, the work is a register of what stood still, and the twelve lives become bands of the studio's star trail, the 41 instruments made between lives dotted

kills.epitaph: Twelve bundles of arcs, rising and setting, drawn a second time below a hero made of arcs. The lives now live where their instruments are: bands of one star-trail sky.
Two businesses side by side under hairlines read as a feature pair. They are a register now, ruled, directly under the man who stood still.
The gold form and the forks, keyed on plate ii. The point of the plate is that they went to mist. Only the name is keyed.
Every reading line leaned. Italic is kept for 'stood still', 'comes back' and Analemma; everywhere else, the words stand upright.
'Held open over all of it, I am mostly sunlight.' The lives say otherwise: forty-one of my instruments were made in the dark between them.
Three lines of mono under the arches told the Barcelona story to nobody. One line keeps the fact; the plate keeps the light.
